extracted.intended_audience: Licensees, spectrum lessees, service providers, FCC applicants, attorneys and compliance officers who file with or transact with the FCC
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements in 47 CFR Part 1 covering Broadband Data Collection corrections, FCC Registration Numbers (FRNs), and spectrum leasing (spectrum manager and de facto transfer leasing arrangements), including definitions, responsibilities, notifications, processing, and enforcement. Targets parties entering into or administering spectrum leases and entities filing with the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband Data Collection: correction filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must file corrections within 30 days of their discovery of incorrect or incomplete data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies whether the error is discovered via self-discovery, crowdsourcing, challenges, Commission verification, or otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband Data Collection: certifications with corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected filings must be accompanied by the same types of certifications that accompany the original filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are not complete unless they include identical certification statements required for original submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to update Broadband Data Collection format
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified FCC offices may update the specific format of data to be submitted pursuant to the Broadband Data Collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of International Affairs, Space Bureau, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, Wireline Competition Bureau, and Office of Economics and Analytics may change GIS/data formats and implement technical improvements or clarifications to filing mechanisms and forms to reflect evolving GIS and data processing functionalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRN: definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC Registration Number (FRN) is a 10-digit unique identifying number that is assigned to entities doing business with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRN uniquely identifies entities in Commission systems and must be used in specified filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain an FRN
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRN is obtained through the Commission Registration System (CORES) on the Internet or by filing FCC Form 160.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CORES link is available at www.fcc.gov; online registration recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must obtain an FRN
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRN must be obtained by anyone doing business with the Commission, including but not limited to specified categories such as payors of statutory charges, license applicants, auction participants, license holders, entities paying on behalf of others, and applicants/service providers in the Schools and Libraries program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to enumerated list (subpart G charges, license applicants, spectrum auction participants, those paying forfeitures, Universal Service Fund contributors, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration information required for FRN
rubrics_metrics.description: When registering for an FRN through CORES, an entity's name, entity type, contact name and title, address, valid email address, and taxpayer identifying number (TIN) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For individuals, the TIN is the Social Security Number (SSN). Registrants must update this information within 10 business days of any change either online or by filing FCC Form 161 (CORES Update/Change Form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple FRNs and subsidiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: A business may obtain as many FRNs as it deems appropriate; each subsidiary with a different TIN must obtain a separate FRN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple FRNs must not be obtained to evade payment of fees or other regulatory responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing the FRN in Commission filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRN must be provided with any filings requiring the payment of statutory charges, license applications, auction participation, contributions to the Universal Service Fund, Schools and Libraries program filings, forfeiture payments, and other listed instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of applications and instances where the FRN is required will be posted on the FCC Internet site and linked to the CORES page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for failure to provide FRN (electronic filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic filing systems for filings that require the FRN will not accept a filing without the appropriate FRN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a filer does not have an FRN, the system will direct the party to CORES to obtain one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for failure to provide FRN (returned/dismissed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided by specific exceptions or other Commission rules, filings subject to the FRN requirement and submitted without an FRN will be returned or dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for exceptions in Commission rules or specific paragraphs that permit correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing/invalid FRN on filing date (no established deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commission has not established a filing deadline for an application, a missing or invalid FRN may be corrected and the application resubmitted; the date the resubmitted application with a valid FRN is received will be considered the official filing date (subject to exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmission should be prompt to avoid loss of filing priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing/invalid FRN on time-sensitive filings/paper filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in certain exceptions, where the Commission has established a filing deadline for an application and that application may be filed on paper, a missing or invalid FRN may be corrected within ten (10) business days of notification to the filer by Commission staff, and if timely corrected the original filing date will be retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ten-business-day correction rule does not apply where other exceptions or rules specify otherwise (e.g., tariff publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: included services for spectrum leasing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectrum leasing policies and rules of this subpart apply to a long list of specified services (e.g., various parts 22, 24, 25, 27, 30, 80, 90, 96, 101 and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation enumerates many services by part and band; consult the list to determine applicability to a particular license/service.

rubrics_metrics.name: De facto control standard for spectrum leasing
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee will be deemed to have retained de facto control of leased spectrum if it enters into a spectrum leasing arrangement and acts as a spectrum manager with regard to portions of the licensed spectrum that it leases, provided the licensee satisfies two specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two conditions relate to (1) licensee responsibility for lessee compliance and (2) licensee responsibility for interactions with the Commission; see related subcriteria for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee responsibility for lessee compliance (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee must remain fully responsible for ensuring the spectrum lessee's compliance with the Communications Act and all applicable policies and rules directly related to the use of the leased spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responsibility is implemented through contractual provisions and active oversight/enforcement, maintaining working knowledge of lessee activities affecting compliance, resolving interference, and exercising rights to inspect and terminate as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee oversight: contractual provisions and actual enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Through contractual provisions and actual oversight and enforcement, the licensee must act in a manner sufficient to ensure the spectrum lessee operates in conformance with applicable technical and use rules governing the license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may use agents (counsel, engineering consultants) if it exercises effective control over agents' actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee operational knowledge and interference responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee must maintain a reasonable degree of actual working knowledge about the spectrum lessee's activities and facilities that affect ongoing compliance, coordinate operations/modifications, make determinations about required applications (e.g., frequency coordination, environmental assessments, international coordination), and ensure compliance with RF safety rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee is responsible for resolving interference matters, including conflicts with other lessees/licensees; may use agents but must exercise effective control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee right to inspect, terminate, and remedy violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee must be able to inspect the spectrum lessee's operations and retain the right to terminate the lease if the lessee fails to comply; the licensee must immediately take steps to remedy violations or harmful interference and enforce compliance using reasonable legal means if lessee refuses to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes suspending or terminating operations or taking other measures until remedied; licensee must act promptly upon Commission or its own determination of violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee responsibility for interactions with the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee remains responsible for filing the necessary notifications and for making all required filings (applications, notifications, correspondence) associated with the license authorization that are directly affected by the spectrum lessee's use of the licensed spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may use agents to prepare filings if it exercises effective control over agent actions and complies with signature requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum manager leasing arrangement: overview and notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee and spectrum lessee may enter into a spectrum manager leasing arrangement without prior Commission approval provided the licensee retains de jure control and de facto control; the licensee must notify the Commission of the arrangement and the term may be no longer than the license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is submitted electronically using ULS and FCC Form 608 (with some manual-file exceptions under § 1.913(d)); designated-entity licensed spectrum may require Commission acceptance prior to commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee rights/responsibilities under spectrum manager lease
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee is directly and primarily responsible for ensuring the spectrum lessee's compliance, must maintain its own eligibility/ownership requirements, and must retain a copy of the spectrum leasing agreement and make it available upon request by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The licensee's accountability to the Commission remains even when operational tasks are performed by a lessee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum lessee rights/responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectrum lessee must comply with the Communications Act and Commission requirements, establish that it meets eligibility and qualification requirements, comply with obligations applicable to it as a service provider, and is independently accountable to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee must cooperate fully with investigations, allow on-site inspections of transmission facilities, suspend operations at Commission or licensee direction when required, and retain a copy of the spectrum leasing agreement for Commission requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference and RF safety rules apply to lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: The interference and radiofrequency (RF) safety rules applicable to use of the spectrum by the licensee as a condition of its license authorization also apply to the use of the spectrum leased by the spectrum lessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes responsibilities to avoid harmful interference and comply with RF exposure rules (e.g., § 1.1307(b) and related rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility requirements for lessees
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum lessee must meet the same eligibility and qualification requirements applicable to the licensee under its license authorization, with specified exceptions for certain public safety and Mobile Satellite Service ATC arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee must meet applicable foreign ownership restrictions (sections 310(a), 310(b)), character qualifications, and must not be subject to denial of Federal benefits under the Anti-Drug Abuse Act; licensee may reasonably rely on lessee's certifications in the notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use restrictions flow to lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent the licensee is restricted from using licensed spectrum to offer particular services under its authorization, those same use restrictions apply to the spectrum lessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee cannot operate outside use restrictions tied to the license authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated entity / entrepreneur rules and leasing
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee subject to designated entity/entrepreneur restrictions or unjust enrichment/transfer restrictions may enter into a spectrum manager leasing arrangement with a lessee regardless of whether the lessee meets designated-entity eligibility, provided the arrangement does not result in the lessee becoming a controlling interest or affiliate that would cause the licensee to lose designated-entity eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangements must not create de facto control or affiliation that undermines the licensee's eligibility status under §§ 1.2110, 1.2111, 24.709, 24.714, 24.839, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and performance/build-out obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any performance or build-out requirement applicable under a license authorization remains a condition of the license and legal responsibility for meeting such obligations is not delegable to the spectrum lessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may attribute lessee activities to itself for compliance; if lessee fails to engage in relied-upon activities, the Commission will enforce requirements against the licensee; licensee remains accountable for discontinuance rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory classification applies to lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the regulatory status of the licensee (e.g., common carrier or non-common carrier) is prescribed by rule, the regulatory status of the spectrum lessee is prescribed in the same manner, subject to limited exceptions (e.g., § 20.9(a) and PMRS/private/non-commercial basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check service-specific rules for classification implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory fees responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee remains responsible for payment of required regulatory fees that must be paid in advance of its license term, but where regulatory fees are paid annually on a per-unit basis, the licensee and spectrum lessee are each required to pay fees for those units associated with their respective operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper apportionment of per-unit fees (e.g., CMRS).

rubrics_metrics.name: E911 obligations for leased spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: If E911 obligations apply to the licensee, the licensee retains those obligations with respect to leased spectrum; however, if the spectrum lessee is a Contraband Interdiction System (CIS) provider, the CIS provider is responsible for compliance with § 9.10(r) regarding E911 transmission obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether the lessee is a CIS provider to determine E911 responsibility allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification filing timing and method
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that seeks to enter into a spectrum manager leasing arrangement must notify the Commission in advance of the spectrum lessee's commencement of operations via ULS using FCC Form 608 (with limited manual-filing exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the license is held pursuant to designated-entity rules and remains subject to unjust enrichment/transfer restrictions, Commission acceptance is required before commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: General notification procedural completeness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: To be accepted under general notification procedures, the notification must be sufficiently complete and contain all information and certifications requested on FCC Form 608 (including eligibility, basic qualifications, and foreign ownership). No application fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee must submit notification at least 21 days in advance of commencing operations unless term is one year or less (then at least 10 days). Notifications are placed on an informational public notice weekly once accepted and are subject to reconsideration (§§ 1.106(f), 1.108, 1.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate processing procedures: qualifying certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for immediate processing, notifications must be complete and, via certification, establish additional qualifications: (A) license does not involve spectrum usable for interconnected mobile services that would create a geographic overlap with spectrum in which the proposed lessee holds a ≥10% direct/indirect interest; (B) licensee is not a designated entity/entrepreneur subject to unjust enrichment/transfer restrictions; (C) arrangement does not require waiver or declaratory ruling of Commission rules; (D) application does not involve Enhanced Competition Incentive Program transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notifications meet these requirements, ULS will reflect acceptance (electronic the next business day; manual upon data entry the next business day) and, once accepted, lessee may commence operations consistent with the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate processing for Contraband Interdiction Systems (CIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee of spectrum used in a CIS qualifies for immediate processing if the notification is sufficiently complete and contains all necessary information and certifications and does not require a waiver or declaratory ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special handling for CIS notifications but same completeness and waiver-free requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and reconsideration for notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications (both general and immediate processing) will be placed on an informational public notice weekly once accepted and are subject to reconsideration under standard procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.933(a) and reconsideration provisions (§§ 1.106(f), 1.108, 1.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of spectrum manager leasing arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum manager leasing arrangement will be deemed effective in Commission records as of the beginning date of the term as specified in the spectrum leasing notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure notification accurately states the commencement date; acceptance in ULS confirms status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission right to investigate and terminate arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may investigate and terminate any spectrum manager leasing arrangement if it determines post-notification that the arrangement constitutes an unauthorized transfer of de facto control, violates rules, or raises foreign ownership, competitive, or other public interest concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information concerning any termination will be placed on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration, extension, and early termination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent Commission termination, a spectrum leasing arrangement expires on the termination date set forth in the notification. Extensions require advance notification per applicable procedures (21 days for general procedures). Early termination requires the licensee to file a notification no later than ten (10) days after the early termination indicating the termination date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions and early terminations will be placed on public notice; extending beyond initial term requires new notification processed under general or immediate procedures as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of a spectrum leasing arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectrum lessee may assign its spectrum leasing arrangement provided the licensee has agreed, is in privity with the assignee, and notifies the Commission before consummation pursuant to applicable notification procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-substantial (pro forma) assignments that fall within pro forma transactions not requiring prior approval under § 1.948(c)(1), the licensee must file notification using FCC Form 608 and provide any necessary ownership updates within 30 days of completion. Commission will place information related to the assignment on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of control of a spectrum lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee must notify the Commission of any transfer of control of a spectrum lessee before consummation pursuant to the applicable notification procedures; pro forma transfers must be notified within 30 days of completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification uses FCC Form 608 and updates ownership information as necessary; requirements align with pro forma transaction rules under § 1.948(c)(1).
